A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same H-embedding guided hypernetwork research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original continual-learning accuracy, ablation, transfer, and timing results, including experiments on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, DomainNet, and PermutedMNIST.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds an ImageNet-R comparison of alternative transferability metrics and task embeddings in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The proposed H-score/AHP embedding construction, hypernetwork, encoder-decoder guidance, losses, LoRA application, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 evaluates alternative substitutions as ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same datasets, task sequences, and TIL/CIL scenarios. The new embedding comparison uses the already covered ImageNet-R ten-task benchmark.

E2.justification: New Table 4 evaluates LEEP-based and LogME-based embedding variants and a Task2Vec replacement against H-embedding. The comparator sets in the retained benchmark and ablation comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented splits, backbones, training budgets, hyperparameters, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 adds variant comparisons under retained benchmark coverage without reporting a separate revision to these settings.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a focused ablation distinguishing replacement of H-score alone from replacement of the entire embedding formulation. Figure 3(a) also revises existing component-ablation results; the earlier convergence and embedding-interpretability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 3(a) is newly described as averaged across seeds. The existing three-run policy, seeds 22/32/42, and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; this clarification does not establish additional runs or new significance testing.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports FAA values of 81.8, 81.6, 81.4, and 79.8 for H-embedding, LEEP, LogME, and Task2Vec respectively. Figure 3(a) changes several ablation values, notably the ten-task w/o Hemb result from about 43% to 77%. The matched earlier tables retain their values, including 42.85% for that entry in v3 Table 5; the discrepancy is unexplained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14, the formal task definitions, and the HGR/self-transferability derivation in Appendix A.2 are retained. The covariance footnote and expanded normalization explanation clarify existing mathematics without adding or revising a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about transferability-aware embeddings, efficient hypernetwork guidance, plug-in flexibility, and continual-learning performance.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly interprets the alternative-metric results as supporting flexibility beyond H-score. It attributes Task2Vec's lower performance to independently constructed embeddings and probe-network dependence. The existing limitations of the CIL task-classifier extension remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access reference changes from an anonymous hosting address to a named GitHub repository. A new footnote clarifies the covariance calculations in Equation 2. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Achille et al. (2019, Task2Vec) and Ermis et al. (2022). It distinguishes prior transferability-based continual learning by its stored-model/sample requirements and expands positioning against alternative embeddings. LEEP and LogME were already cited in v2.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized explanatory edits, adds Appendix A.3 and specific appendix cross-references, and updates the title and author information. It also adds funding acknowledgments and a conference checklist. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 4, redraws Figure 3, changes its CIL axis to percentages, and revises its caption. The author block and appendix floats are rearranged. Earlier Tables 4–6 become Tables 5–7, while Figures 1, 2, 4, and 5 retain their graphics.

improvement.justification: The new alternative-embedding comparison and discussion improve the design justification, and Figure 3 now aligns the proposed-method and SD-LoRA values with the main comparison tables. However, the revised ten-task w/o Hemb result is about 77% while Appendix Table 5 still reports 42.85%, without reconciling their aggregation. The new comparison also lacks variant-specific settings and uncertainty estimates. These gains and unresolved reporting issues prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality improvement.
